pathway.title: Phinia Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate: LTM sales of USD 3,619 million, 62.05% of nine-month 2026 sales in vehicle-facing Power Systems and 37.95% in aftermarket-facing Aftermarket Solutions, with General Motors 18% of FY2025 sales and 63% of sales outside the United States. Combustion and hybrid products and a customer at 18% of sales make the profile cyclical, so scale supports debt service only while vehicle volumes and the largest customer hold. Basis: calculation Q1; calculation Q7; calculation Q18; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

Aftermarket Solutions is the main credit support because it earns the higher margin and a disproportionate share of profit: 17.1% segment margin against 10.8% at Power Systems, and 49.17% of segment adjusted operating income from 37.95% of sales in the nine months of 2026. Management says growth in the vehicle parc supports aftermarket demand, so this profit pool should be less tied to new-vehicle build rates, although the filings give no aftermarket volumes through a downturn. Basis: calculation Q7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50

Margin resilience is average, because recent profit growth leans on tariff timing and currency. Reported EBITDA rose from USD 420 million in FY2023 to USD 430 million in FY2024 while net sales fell 2.77%, which shows cost control in a soft year, but in FY2025 gross profit rose only USD 6 million on USD 80 million of extra sales, because currency added USD 36 million while volume and mix took USD 23 million and employee costs USD 17 million. In the nine months of 2026 tariff items supplied USD 17 million of the USD 39 million gross profit increase, in a period when cost of sales included a benefit from one-time tariff refunds. Basis: calculation Q2; calculation Q3; calculation Q4; calculation Q5; calculation Q22

Cash conversion is positive but uneven, and shareholder returns are the swing factor. Free cash flow was USD 100 million in FY2023, USD 203 million in FY2024 and USD 188 million in FY2025, which is 23.81%, 47.21% and 44.55% of reported EBITDA, and capital expenditure fell from USD 150 million to USD 100 million over the last twelve months. Dividends and buybacks of USD 244 million in FY2025 and USD 198 million in the nine months of 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 188 million and USD 160 million, and the excess falls to USD 32 million and USD 9 million on the company's adjusted measure. Basis: calculation Q9; calculation Q10; calculation Q11; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

Leverage is moderate and has risen through policy rather than weaker earnings. Net debt to reported EBITDA rose from 1.03x in FY2023 to 1.45x in FY2025 and was 1.35x at 30 September 2026 as last-twelve-months EBITDA grew, or 1.64x after the USD 136 million stoba purchase paid on 1 October 2026; cash interest cover was 7.46x on a net basis that overstates cover. The pro forma ratio excludes stoba's own earnings and any debt it carries, which are not established, and the issuer's own net leverage was 1.32x on adjusted EBITDA. Basis: calculation Q12; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

Liquidity is Strong before the stoba payment and the first real refinancing pressure arrives in 2028. Liquidity of USD 813 million, combining USD 436 million of cash and USD 377 million of undrawn revolver, was measured before the USD 136 million payment and is not established after it, and 82.80% of the cash sits in foreign subsidiaries. The revolver, drawn USD 123 million, matures in July 2028, about 19 months away, followed by the USD 525 million 2029 secured notes and the USD 450 million 2032 notes. Basis: calculation Q15; calculation Q16; calculation Q13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

Governance adds a moderate policy risk rather than a structural one. No controlling shareholder or sponsor is identified and the audit opinion is unqualified, but returns that match or exceed free cash flow and a debt-assisted acquisition, with the payout limits in the debt agreements not supplied, keep the governance rating at Medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation Q11

cells.text: Designs and makes fuel injection systems, fuel delivery modules, sensors and electronic controls for combustion and hybrid propulsion, plus original equipment service and independent aftermarket products

Two reportable segments: Fuel Systems and Aftermarket until 2026-08-31; Power Systems and Aftermarket Solutions from 2026-09-01. Most of the OES business moved from Aftermarket to Fuel Systems in Q4 2025 and prior periods were recast
Fuel Systems USD 2,177 million (62.50%) and Aftermarket USD 1,306 million (37.50%) of USD 3,483 million net sales to customers; segment AOI USD 244 million and USD 211 million
Power Systems USD 1,694 million (62.05%) and Aftermarket Solutions USD 1,036 million (37.95%) of USD 2,730 million; segment AOI USD 183 million and USD 177 million, margins 10.8% and 17.1%
Service (OES and IAM) about 35%, light passenger vehicle 25%, light commercial vehicle 19%, medium and heavy duty 15%, off-highway, industrial and other 6%
Americas USD 1,486 million (42.66%), Europe USD 1,391 million (39.94%), Asia USD 606 million (17.40%); the United States was 37% and outside the United States 63% of net sales

General Motors was 18% of net sales in FY2025 (17% in FY2024, 16% in FY2023); the top five customers were 37%; no other customer exceeded 10%; most OEM sales run on negotiated annual contracts or long-term supply agreements

25 principal manufacturing, assembly and technical facilities at 2025-12-31, 17 of them leased sites; headquarters leased in Auburn Hills, Michigan; 12,500 employees at 2025-12-31 (Americas 5,500, Europe 5,300, Asia 1,700); about 13,500 employees and 21 countries in the Q3 2026 company description
Net R&D cost USD 105 million in FY2025 (3.0% of net sales) after USD 85 million of customer reimbursements on USD 190 million gross
Many competitors, including Robert Bosch, Cummins, Denso and Hitachi Astemo, are larger and better resourced; competition is on price, quality, delivery, technology and launch support
Delphi-TVS Diesel Systems Ltd (India), 52.5% owned but equity-accounted; joint venture sales were about USD 256 million in FY2025 and equity earnings USD 15 million
Contract manufacturing agreements reduced Fuel Systems net sales by USD 23 million in FY2025; the spin-off also created contract manufacturing agreements with BorgWarner

runs.text: The aftermarket arm is the first strength. It earns a 17.1% segment margin and 49.17% of segment adjusted operating income from 37.95% of sales in the nine months of 2026, and management ties its demand to the growing vehicle parc, so it cushions group cash flow when new-vehicle production softens and supports debt service. Basis: calculation Q7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50

Cash generation through a soft year is the second strength. Reported EBITDA rose from USD 420 million to USD 430 million in FY2024 as net sales fell, free cash flow stayed positive in every period shown, and capital expenditure fell by a third from FY2023 to the last twelve months, so spending can be cut to protect cash if conditions worsen. Basis: calculation Q2; calculation Q3; calculation Q9; calculation Q10

Debt structure is the third strength. No sizeable principal falls due before the revolver matures in July 2028, and the 2029 secured notes and 2032 notes are fixed-rate with a 6.7% weighted average rate on all borrowings, so near-term refinancing pressure is low. Basis: calculation Q14; calculation Q15; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

Moderate leverage and cover are the fourth strength. Net debt was 1.35x reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, or 1.64x after the stoba purchase paid on 1 October 2026, and cash interest cover was 7.46x on a net basis, so the profile can absorb a moderate EBITDA decline before debt service is stressed. Basis: calculation Q12; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Shareholder returns above free cash flow are the first weakness. Returns exceeded free cash flow by USD 56 million in FY2025 and USD 38 million in the nine months of 2026, and net leverage rose from 1.03x to 1.45x between FY2023 and FY2025, so continued returns above cash generation would keep adding leverage. Basis: calculation Q11; calculation Q12

Earnings quality is the second weakness. Tariff items supplied the whole USD 17 million increase in nine-month segment adjusted operating income and USD 17 million of the USD 39 million gross profit increase, and the tariff line includes one-time refunds, so part of the improvement may not recur and could reverse as refunds are returned to customers. Basis: calculation Q5; calculation Q6; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

Customer and technology concentration is the third weakness. General Motors is 18% of sales and the top five customers 37%, and the risk factors name faster electric-vehicle adoption as an adverse case for combustion-linked products, so a loss of volume at one customer or an earlier powertrain shift would hit Power Systems first. Basis: calculation Q18; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33

Debt-assisted acquisition with undisclosed target financials is the fourth weakness. The USD 136 million stoba purchase was paid from cash that included revolver borrowings, and no source states stoba's own debt or earnings, so leverage after the purchase is bounded only by the stated price. Basis: calculation Q12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Phinia became independent on 3 July 2023, when BorgWarner distributed all of its shares to BorgWarner holders, one for every five held on 23 June 2023, and the company entered a USD 1,225 million credit agreement the same day. That agreement combined a USD 500 million revolver, a USD 300 million Term Loan A and a USD 425 million Term Loan B, and matures on 3 July 2028. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

The only new debt issues in the supplied filings are the two 2024 notes. On 4 April 2024 the company issued USD 525 million of senior secured notes due 2029, which are guaranteed by certain domestic restricted subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets, ranking equally with the credit facilities, and used the proceeds to repay the Term Loan B and revolver borrowings. On 17 September 2024 it issued USD 450 million of senior unsecured notes due 2032 and repaid the Term Loan A. The same two dates brought Amendment No. 1, which raised the net leverage covenant from 3.00x to 3.25x with a step-up to 3.75x after a qualifying acquisition, and Amendment No. 2, which cut the revolver margin. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation K16

No further notes were issued in 2025 or 2026 to date. The USD 24 million of 5.0% senior notes assumed at the spin-off was repaid in full on 1 October 2025, and the revolver, undrawn at the end of 2025, stood at USD 123 million drawn at 30 September 2026 after borrowing ahead of the stoba closing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

The stoba Group agreement was signed on 30 June 2026 at an expected price of about USD 150 million, to be funded from available liquidity, and the purchase closed on 1 October 2026 for USD 136 million financed from cash on hand including revolver proceeds. The earlier acquisition, of Swedish Electromagnet on 1 August 2025, cost USD 46 million after a USD 1 million price adjustment, with USD 32 million of assumed debt repaid at closing. The closing falls after the 30 September 2026 balance sheet, so no period figure in this module includes stoba. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_phin-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation K12; calculation K13

The October 2025 settlement with BorgWarner ended the Delaware dispute over tax matters agreement refunds. It requires USD 31 million paid in Q4 2025, USD 21 million paid in Q1 2026 and a final USD 26 million over 2026 as refunds arrive, cost a USD 39 million loss in FY2025, and was accompanied by an amended tax matters agreement that lets the company use pre-spin credits worth up to about USD 29 million in cash. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; calculation K14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Phinia Inc. (issuer id phin-1968915), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module builds the financial foundation from the eight supplied issuer filings and earnings releases: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and interest cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate and no material term debt matures before 2029, so the main creditor exposure is the stoba purchase that closed after the balance-sheet date, not refinancing. Total debt was 2.25x and net debt 1.35x reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, before the USD 136 million purchase lifted net debt to USD 793 million, or 1.64x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R1; calculation R2; calculation P1; calculation P2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover was 7.46x on a net-of-interest-received basis that overstates cover, and adjusted EBITDA is stated only from FY2025, so adjusted ratios rest on one full-year figure of USD 478 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage on reported EBITDA rose from 1.03x in FY2023 to 1.45x in FY2025 and was 1.35x at 30 September 2026, because net debt grew from USD 433 million to USD 657 million while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA moved from USD 420 million to USD 485 million. The main driver is shareholder return rather than weaker earnings: dividends and treasury stock purchases were USD 244 million in FY2025 against free cash flow of USD 188 million, and USD 198 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 160 million, so the gap was funded from cash and the revolver and net debt rose. For creditors this means leverage is a policy outcome that management can move either way, and the next test is whether the stoba purchase is followed by lower returns or by further borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N1; calculation N6; calculation M3; calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on cash interest paid fell from 16.15x in FY2023 to 7.15x in FY2025 and was 7.46x on a last-twelve-months basis. The fall reflects gross debt rising from USD 798 million to USD 970 million as the 2024 notes replaced term loans, and FY2023 cash interest covers only part of a year under the post-spin-off capital structure. The measure is net of interest received, so it overstates cover against gross cash interest, which the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R3; calculation I3; calculation D1; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence to a moderate view is the pace of shareholder returns and the acquisition after quarter end: both lift net debt without a matching rise in earnings, and the pro forma figure excludes the acquired business's own cash, debt and EBITDA, which no source states. A cut in buybacks, or a stoba contribution that lifts EBITDA as the revised full-year guidance assumes, would strengthen the view; a further debt-funded acquisition or a revolver balance that stays drawn would weaken it. Covenant definitions are not supplied, so no covenant headroom is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation P1; calculation P2; calculation F3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 312 million in FY2025, about 74% of reported EBITDA, and capital expenditure of USD 124 million left free cash flow of USD 188 million. In the nine months of 2026 free cash flow was USD 160 million against USD 121 million a year earlier, because operating cash flow was USD 15 million higher and capital expenditure USD 24 million lower. Free cash flow after interest therefore covers dividends but not dividends and buybacks together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; calculation F4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was USD 436 million of cash and USD 377 million of undrawn revolver, and the revolver had been drawn to USD 123 million ahead of the stoba payment, so the cash includes borrowed money that was paid out on 1 October 2026. Of the cash, USD 361 million is held by subsidiaries outside the United States, and the filings do not say whether it is restricted. Liquidity after the payment is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Term debt is long-dated: the schedule at 31 December 2025 shows USD 3 million due in 2026, USD 1 million in 2027, USD 1 million in 2028, USD 526 million in 2029 and USD 450 million in 2032. The revolver, USD 123 million drawn at 30 September 2026, matures in July 2028, so the first material maturity after the revolver is the 2029 secured notes. No schedule at 30 September 2026 is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is the issuer's unadjusted EBITDA: stated in the releases for the quarters and nine-month periods, and built from statement components for the fiscal years with the same definition, which reproduces the issuer's figures for both nine-month periods. The issuer's net leverage of 1.3x divides net debt by trailing adjusted EBITDA and is 1.32x on our calculation; on reported EBITDA it is 1.35x. The gap is the issuer's add-backs, mainly restructuring and merger costs, which leave adjusted EBITDA USD 11 million above reported on a last-twelve-months basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation E4; calculation C2; calculation B1; calculation B2; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three definition differences are kept visible rather than reconciled: cash paid for interest is net of interest received, the FY2024 annual report shows restructuring inside other operating expense while the FY2025 report splits it out, and the revolver draws appear on two cash flow lines whose split the filings do not state. None changes a leverage figure, but the first overstates interest cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent event: the stoba Group acquisition closed on 2026-10-01 for USD 136 million, after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet; it is kept out of every period figure and shown only in the post-balance-sheet table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The four rows add to total debt of USD 1,093 million at 30 September 2026 (123 plus 521 plus 445 plus 4), the carrying value on the balance sheet. The weighted average interest rate on all borrowings was 6.7% at 31 December 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The figures use reported EBITDA, not the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, and the 2026-09-30 row precedes the stoba payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest is paid net of interest received, so each figure overstates cover relative to gross cash interest, and FY2023 precedes a full year under the current capital structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash at 2026-09-30 includes revolver borrowings drawn to fund the stoba purchase paid on 2026-10-01, so the 2026-09-30 row overstates liquidity after that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The schedule is at 2025-12-31, the latest supplied; it does not include the USD 123 million revolver draw at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The EBITDA column is reported EBITDA, not the issuer's adjusted measure, which is stated for FY2025 and 2026 periods only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Finance leases of USD 4 million are inside total debt but left out because no source states their rank or security.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge is for nine months 2026 because the issuer prints no full-year reconciliation for FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each calculation below shows its inputs and result in USD million unless stated, and every ratio is rounded half up to two decimals from the exact quotient.

fields.value: - Adjusted EBITDA is not stated for FY2023 or FY2024, and FY2025 appears only as a single total of USD 478 million in the third-quarter release, so adjusted leverage and cover for FY2023 and FY2024 are not supplied and the adjusted trend rests on one full-year figure; severity High; the fourth-quarter 2025 release or reconciliations for FY2024 and FY2025 would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported EBITDA for FY2023 to FY2025 is built from statement components because the annual reports do not state it; the same build reproduces the issuer's stated EBITDA for both nine-month periods, so severity is Medium; a stated FY2025 EBITDA would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The only maturity schedules are at 2025-12-31 and 2024-12-31, so the debt maturity chart does not show the USD 123 million revolver draw at 2026-09-30 or its July 2028 maturity; severity High; a schedule at 2026-09-30 would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The stoba purchase closed on 2026-10-01, after the latest balance sheet, and no source states stoba's own cash, debt or EBITDA, cash paid net of cash acquired, or liquidity after closing, so the pro forma net debt and leverage are limited to the USD 136 million price on the stated EBITDA; severity High; the issuer's closing balance sheet or pro forma figures would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash paid for interest is printed net of interest received, so interest cover on cash interest overstates cover against gross interest paid, and the first quarter of 2026 and 2025 show net receipts that cannot be stated as cash interest paid; severity Medium; gross interest paid would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Availability under the revolver at 2023-12-31 is not stated, only USD 75 million of borrowings, so the FY2023 undrawn facilities cell is not supplied; severity Low; the FY2023 annual report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Several cash flow and income statement lines are printed as a dash or are absent from one statement while present in another (for example the revolver and short-term borrowing lines in the nine-month statement, the debt issuance lines in the annual statement, and other postretirement expense in FY2024), and stock-based compensation is not stated for the third quarter; these cells are not supplied and are never read as zero; severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The revolver's margin, reference rate, floor and scheduled amortisation are not stated in the supplied sources, nor are the finance leases' rank, security and principal, so those cells are not supplied and the finance leases are left out of the debt stack; severity Medium; the credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings do not say which cash flow line carries the USD 123 million revolver balance: borrowings and repayments are USD 80 million each and the net increase in short-term borrowings is USD 121 million; severity Low; the figures are shown as printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The adjusted EBITDA margin for FY2023 and FY2024 and the United States share of net sales for FY2023 and FY2024 are not stated in the supplied reports, so those dashboard cells are not supplied; severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Letters of credit under the revolver are not stated, so undrawn facilities equal the issuer's stated availability and are not reduced for any letter of credit; severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Phinia Inc. (issuer id phin-1968915), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module states the business, transaction, ownership and governance facts that matter to creditors, from the eight supplied issuer filings and releases and the Source readiness findings. It makes no valuation, peer, recovery or instrument conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Phinia has no controlling owner or sponsor in the supplied filings, so governance risk to creditors lies in management's capital allocation, rated Medium because shareholder returns have matched or exceeded free cash flow and the debt agreements' payout limits are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aftermarket Solutions earned 49.17% of the USD 360 million of segment adjusted operating income in the nine months of 2026 on 37.95% of sales, so profit leans further toward aftermarket sales than the revenue split does. The USD 136 million stoba purchase, paid from cash on hand that included revolver borrowings, closed on 1 October 2026, after the latest balance sheet, and no source states its own debt or earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation K2; calculation K3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is dispersed and no controlling shareholder or sponsor is identified, so there is no sponsor support or extraction to underwrite and creditor protection rests on the debt agreements and on management's policy. The spin-off distributed all shares to BorgWarner's stockholders on 3 July 2023, and BorgWarner has been a counterparty rather than an owner since. Beneficial-ownership and board-independence disclosure sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a large holder cannot be ruled out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the main policy risk. Dividends and buybacks were USD 244 million against free cash flow of USD 188 million in FY2025 and USD 198 million against USD 160 million in the nine months of 2026, so returns exceeded free cash flow by USD 56 million and USD 38 million. The gap narrows on the company's adjusted free cash flow, which adds back separation-related payments, to USD 32 million in FY2025 and USD 9 million in the nine months of 2026, so returns have run at or slightly above cash generation rather than far ahead of it. Each excess reduces the cash cushion or adds debt, and USD 151 million of the USD 750 million buyback authorisation remained at 30 September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9; calculation K18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating mix tilts creditor risk toward vehicle-programme cycles in the larger segment, offset by an aftermarket arm with a higher margin. Power Systems earned a 10.8% segment margin and Aftermarket Solutions 17.1% in the nine months of 2026; General Motors was 18% of FY2025 net sales, the top five customers 37%, and 63% of sales were outside the United States.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition appetite has widened and the latest deal is debt-assisted. The USD 46 million Swedish Electromagnet purchase in 2025 was followed by the USD 136 million stoba purchase on 1 October 2026, financed from cash on hand that included revolver borrowings drawn and outstanding at 30 September 2026. The price was USD 14 million below the roughly USD 150 million expected on 30 June 2026, for a reason the filings do not give, and stoba's own debt, earnings and integration plan are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The separation legacy is settled but not finished. The October 2025 settlement with BorgWarner commits USD 78 million of payments; the final USD 26 million is paid over 2026 as the company receives indirect-tax refunds, and the company expects a substantial portion of the payments to be funded from those refunds. USD 53 million was still due from BorgWarner at 30 September 2026 against USD 68 million at the end of 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is sound but in transition. PricewaterhouseCoopers gave unqualified opinions on the FY2025 statements and on internal control, with one critical audit matter on goodwill of the Fuel Systems reporting unit, which carries USD 71 million of the USD 509 million total. A new SAP system went live during the third quarter of 2026 and changed financial-reporting controls, and the first quarter that consolidates stoba is the next to be reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt terms support a seniority view but cannot be tested for payout capacity. The 2029 secured notes rank equally with the first-priority security of the credit facilities and the 2032 notes are unsecured; the annual report quotes a 3.25x net leverage covenant, 3.75x after a qualifying acquisition, and 3.00x interest cover. The executed agreements are not supplied, so the restricted-payment, investment and lien baskets that govern buybacks and acquisitions are not established, and the annual report states that none of the debt agreements requires accelerated repayment on a downgrade.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against Medium is that Phinia looks conservatively run: no related-party transactions since the spin-off, no exchange, priming or asset transfer that moved value away from creditors in any supplied filing, unqualified audit opinions, and a third quarter in which management says capital returned was 104% of adjusted free cash flow, close to what the business generated. On the adjusted measure the nine-month excess was only USD 9 million, so Low would be defensible. Medium stays because the net leverage covenant ceiling was raised from 3.00x to 3.25x in 2024 when the notes replaced the term loans, a debt-assisted acquisition came while the buyback programme was running, and the documents that would show what the company may pay out or borrow are absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation K11; calculation K18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to Low if the executed agreements show tight restricted-payment baskets and a leverage covenant with real headroom after stoba. It would move to High if buybacks continue above free cash flow while the revolver stays drawn, or if the company used unrestricted-subsidiary, priming or exchange mechanics, none of which any supplied source reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee roles, beneficial owners and pay design are not established; the Medium rating therefore rests on disclosed conduct only, and an independent board or a named large holder would lower or raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for restricted payments, investments and liens is not established; the separation of capacity from willingness stays open and loose baskets would raise the rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Stoba's own debt, earnings and cash are not stated, so the acquisition-appetite judgement cannot be sized beyond its USD 136 million price and may be too benign if stoba carries debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reported-line comparison treats USD 29 million of separation-related payments in the nine months of 2026 as ordinary outflows; on the issuer's adjusted measure the gap shrinks to USD 9 million, so the returns-driven part of the Medium rating could fall away if returns settle at or below adjusted free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The rating statement dates from the February 2026 annual report and no agency report is supplied, so the view of financial policy cannot be checked against a current agency opinion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Phinia became independent on 3 July 2023, when BorgWarner distributed all of its shares to BorgWarner holders, one for every five held on 23 June 2023, and the company entered a USD 1,225 million credit agreement the same day. That agreement combined a USD 500 million revolver, a USD 300 million Term Loan A and a USD 425 million Term Loan B, and matures on 3 July 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt issues in the supplied filings are the two 2024 notes. On 4 April 2024 the company issued USD 525 million of senior secured notes due 2029, which are guaranteed by certain domestic restricted subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets, ranking equally with the credit facilities, and used the proceeds to repay the Term Loan B and revolver borrowings. On 17 September 2024 it issued USD 450 million of senior unsecured notes due 2032 and repaid the Term Loan A. The same two dates brought Amendment No. 1, which raised the net leverage covenant from 3.00x to 3.25x with a step-up to 3.75x after a qualifying acquisition, and Amendment No. 2, which cut the revolver margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation K16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No further notes were issued in 2025 or 2026 to date. The USD 24 million of 5.0% senior notes assumed at the spin-off was repaid in full on 1 October 2025, and the revolver, undrawn at the end of 2025, stood at USD 123 million drawn at 30 September 2026 after borrowing ahead of the stoba closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The stoba Group agreement was signed on 30 June 2026 at an expected price of about USD 150 million, to be funded from available liquidity, and the purchase closed on 1 October 2026 for USD 136 million financed from cash on hand including revolver proceeds. The earlier acquisition, of Swedish Electromagnet on 1 August 2025, cost USD 46 million after a USD 1 million price adjustment, with USD 32 million of assumed debt repaid at closing. The closing falls after the 30 September 2026 balance sheet, so no period figure in this module includes stoba.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_phin-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation K12; calculation K13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The October 2025 settlement with BorgWarner ended the Delaware dispute over tax matters agreement refunds. It requires USD 31 million paid in Q4 2025, USD 21 million paid in Q1 2026 and a final USD 26 million over 2026 as refunds arrive, cost a USD 39 million loss in FY2025, and was accompanied by an amended tax matters agreement that lets the company use pre-spin credits worth up to about USD 29 million in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by returns that exceed free cash flow and a debt-assisted acquisition, because both draw on the cash cushion, which implies higher leverage and weaker liquidity if they continue; countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, related-party leakage or adverse amendment, and clean audit opinions. Further analysis requires the executed debt agreements and the proxy statement.

fields.value: Phinia Inc. (issuer id phin-1968915), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Phinia's fundamental credit profile is adequate: a higher-margin aftermarket arm, moderate leverage and no sizeable maturity before July 2028 support debt service, but creditors depend on management holding shareholder returns to free cash flow after the stoba purchase.

fields.value: Basis: calculation Q7; calculation Q12; calculation Q14; calculation Q11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage was 1.35x at 30 September 2026 on reported EBITDA, or 1.64x after the USD 136 million stoba purchase paid on 1 October 2026, and USD 813 million of liquidity was measured before that payment, while the figure after it is not established. The primary downside path is a softer original-equipment market while tariff-timing gains reverse and buybacks continue, which would lift leverage ahead of the 2028 revolver and 2029 note maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q12; calculation Q16; calculation Q5; calculation Q15; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: LTM sales of USD 3,619 million, 62.05% of nine-month 2026 sales in vehicle-facing Power Systems and 37.95% in aftermarket-facing Aftermarket Solutions, with General Motors 18% of FY2025 sales and 63% of sales outside the United States. Combustion and hybrid products and a customer at 18% of sales make the profile cyclical, so scale supports debt service only while vehicle volumes and the largest customer hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q1; calculation Q7; calculation Q18; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aftermarket Solutions is the main credit support because it earns the higher margin and a disproportionate share of profit: 17.1% segment margin against 10.8% at Power Systems, and 49.17% of segment adjusted operating income from 37.95% of sales in the nine months of 2026. Management says growth in the vehicle parc supports aftermarket demand, so this profit pool should be less tied to new-vehicle build rates, although the filings give no aftermarket volumes through a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is average, because recent profit growth leans on tariff timing and currency. Reported EBITDA rose from USD 420 million in FY2023 to USD 430 million in FY2024 while net sales fell 2.77%, which shows cost control in a soft year, but in FY2025 gross profit rose only USD 6 million on USD 80 million of extra sales, because currency added USD 36 million while volume and mix took USD 23 million and employee costs USD 17 million. In the nine months of 2026 tariff items supplied USD 17 million of the USD 39 million gross profit increase, in a period when cost of sales included a benefit from one-time tariff refunds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q2; calculation Q3; calculation Q4; calculation Q5; calculation Q22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is positive but uneven, and shareholder returns are the swing factor. Free cash flow was USD 100 million in FY2023, USD 203 million in FY2024 and USD 188 million in FY2025, which is 23.81%, 47.21% and 44.55% of reported EBITDA, and capital expenditure fell from USD 150 million to USD 100 million over the last twelve months. Dividends and buybacks of USD 244 million in FY2025 and USD 198 million in the nine months of 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 188 million and USD 160 million, and the excess falls to USD 32 million and USD 9 million on the company's adjusted measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q9; calculation Q10; calculation Q11; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate and has risen through policy rather than weaker earnings. Net debt to reported EBITDA rose from 1.03x in FY2023 to 1.45x in FY2025 and was 1.35x at 30 September 2026 as last-twelve-months EBITDA grew, or 1.64x after the USD 136 million stoba purchase paid on 1 October 2026; cash interest cover was 7.46x on a net basis that overstates cover. The pro forma ratio excludes stoba's own earnings and any debt it carries, which are not established, and the issuer's own net leverage was 1.32x on adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q12; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is Strong before the stoba payment and the first real refinancing pressure arrives in 2028. Liquidity of USD 813 million, combining USD 436 million of cash and USD 377 million of undrawn revolver, was measured before the USD 136 million payment and is not established after it, and 82.80% of the cash sits in foreign subsidiaries. The revolver, drawn USD 123 million, matures in July 2028, about 19 months away, followed by the USD 525 million 2029 secured notes and the USD 450 million 2032 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q15; calculation Q16; calculation Q13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance adds a moderate policy risk rather than a structural one. No controlling shareholder or sponsor is identified and the audit opinion is unqualified, but returns that match or exceed free cash flow and a debt-assisted acquisition, with the payout limits in the debt agreements not supplied, keep the governance rating at Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that Phinia has stayed cash generative, kept net leverage near 1.3x on the issuer's own definition before the stoba purchase and holds BB+ and Ba1 ratings with stable outlooks as stated in the FY2025 annual report. Free cash flow covered dividends in every year shown and reported EBITDA rose in FY2024 through a sales decline, so the profile could be called strong. That case loses force because profit growth in 2026 rests on tariff timing and currency, one customer is 18% of sales, the history holds only one mild decline, and the covenant definitions that would test leverage are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q3; calculation Q5; calculation Q6; calculation Q9; calculation Q12; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the first full stoba quarter adds EBITDA without further revolver drawing, returns stay at or below adjusted free cash flow, and the July 2028 revolver is extended well before maturity. It would weaken if the tariff gains reverse, Power Systems margin falls below its 10.8% level, or buybacks continue while the revolver stays drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q6; calculation Q8; calculation Q11; calculation Q15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set, agency report, market quote or sector dataset is supplied, so the adequate profile is judged against Phinia's own history and risk factors; comparable issuers or a current agency view could move it up or down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The supplied history holds one mild volume decline and no severe downturn, so the margin and cash-conversion judgement has not been tested by a deep cycle; a steeper fall in sales would weaken it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No source states stoba's own earnings, debt or cash, or the company's position after the payment, so the leverage and liquidity conclusions carry a one-quarter lag and leverage after the purchase could differ from the pro forma 1.64x in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant definitions and headroom are not available, so moderate leverage is measured against the company's own ratios and not against a maintenance test; a tight definition could make the covenant the binding constraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The aftermarket arm is the first strength. It earns a 17.1% segment margin and 49.17% of segment adjusted operating income from 37.95% of sales in the nine months of 2026, and management ties its demand to the growing vehicle parc, so it cushions group cash flow when new-vehicle production softens and supports debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation through a soft year is the second strength. Reported EBITDA rose from USD 420 million to USD 430 million in FY2024 as net sales fell, free cash flow stayed positive in every period shown, and capital expenditure fell by a third from FY2023 to the last twelve months, so spending can be cut to protect cash if conditions worsen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q2; calculation Q3; calculation Q9; calculation Q10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt structure is the third strength. No sizeable principal falls due before the revolver matures in July 2028, and the 2029 secured notes and 2032 notes are fixed-rate with a 6.7% weighted average rate on all borrowings, so near-term refinancing pressure is low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q14; calculation Q15; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Moderate leverage and cover are the fourth strength. Net debt was 1.35x reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, or 1.64x after the stoba purchase paid on 1 October 2026, and cash interest cover was 7.46x on a net basis, so the profile can absorb a moderate EBITDA decline before debt service is stressed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns above free cash flow are the first weakness. Returns exceeded free cash flow by USD 56 million in FY2025 and USD 38 million in the nine months of 2026, and net leverage rose from 1.03x to 1.45x between FY2023 and FY2025, so continued returns above cash generation would keep adding leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the second weakness. Tariff items supplied the whole USD 17 million increase in nine-month segment adjusted operating income and USD 17 million of the USD 39 million gross profit increase, and the tariff line includes one-time refunds, so part of the improvement may not recur and could reverse as refunds are returned to customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q5; calculation Q6; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and technology concentration is the third weakness. General Motors is 18% of sales and the top five customers 37%, and the risk factors name faster electric-vehicle adoption as an adverse case for combustion-linked products, so a loss of volume at one customer or an earlier powertrain shift would hit Power Systems first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q18; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt-assisted acquisition with undisclosed target financials is the fourth weakness. The USD 136 million stoba purchase was paid from cash that included revolver borrowings, and no source states stoba's own debt or earnings, so leverage after the purchase is bounded only by the stated price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Phinia is a standalone, listed maker of fuel systems, electrical systems and aftermarket products, spun off from BorgWarner on 3 July 2023, with two reportable segments, Power Systems and Aftermarket Solutions after a 1 September 2026 rename. No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, the former parent is a counterparty to a settlement and tax agreement rather than an owner, and the debt is issued by the parent with guarantees from certain domestic restricted subsidiaries, so creditor protection rests on the debt agreements and on management policy more than on owner support. The 52.5% joint venture in India is equity-accounted and not controlled, so its earnings reach creditors as equity income rather than consolidated cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and partly pass-through rather than recurring. OEM sales run on negotiated annual contracts and long-term supply agreements subject to production schedules, and the FY2025 sales increase of USD 80 million came from tariff recovery of USD 38 million and currency and other of USD 45 million while volume and mix were USD 2 million negative. Pricing power is limited: customer pricing added USD 2 million in FY2025 and took USD 7 million off the nine months of 2026, and tariff recoveries are contractual pass-throughs that earn no margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q22; calculation Q27; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost structure gives a margin that is defended rather than expanded. Reported EBITDA margin was 12.00% in FY2023, 12.64% in FY2024 and 12.12% in FY2025, and 13.40% over the last twelve months, with supplier-cost savings of USD 25 million offsetting employee-cost increases of USD 25 million in the nine months of 2026. Net research cost of USD 105 million is partly customer-funded, with 44.74% of gross R&D reimbursed, and unallocated corporate cost took 22.86% of segment adjusted operating income in FY2025, so fixed overhead limits how far margins fall with volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q3; calculation Q5; calculation Q19; calculation Q20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and flexible, so EBITDA converts into free cash flow at 44.55% in FY2025 and 46.80% over the last twelve months, against 23.81% in FY2023 when capital expenditure was USD 150 million. Capital expenditure of USD 100 million over the last twelve months leaves room to cut spending, but the nine-month 2026 operating cash flow benefited from lower spending while third-quarter operating cash flow fell USD 32 million on withholding tax on cash repatriation and receivables timing. Receivables sold without recourse were 4.65% of FY2025 net sales, and the company says it does not depend on them for liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q9; calculation Q10; calculation Q23; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high: major competitors including Robert Bosch, Cummins and Denso are larger and have more diverse portfolios, so price pressure and the need for continued research spending limit margin expansion. Entry barriers are moderate, supported by the company's patents and long-term supply agreements, which reduces the threat of new entrants. The substitution threat is the main long-run risk, because faster electric-vehicle adoption would shrink combustion-linked demand, although management cites hybrids, alternative fuels and aerospace and defence as offsets. Buyer power sits with a few OEMs, led by General Motors at 18% of sales, and customers often expect annual price reductions; supplier power is limited by dual sourcing and long-term contracts, supplier concentration is not stated, and supplier costs were a USD 25 million benefit in the nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation Q5; calculation Q18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy, currency and technology are the external factors that change credit outcomes. Tariffs change both sales and gross profit and refunds from the federal government are expected with uncertain timing; 63% of sales are outside the United States, and currency and other added USD 45 million to FY2025 sales and USD 64 million to the nine months of 2026; and electrification is the technology risk. Credit-translated, the strengths are the aftermarket arm and cash generation, the weaknesses are returns above free cash flow and tariff-dependent earnings, the opportunities are alternative fuels, aerospace and defence and commercial-vehicle share gains, and the threats are faster electrification, reversing tariff gains and a softer original-equipment market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation Q22; calculation Q27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: We assess scale and market position as Average, because LTM sales of USD 3,619 million are meaningful but several competitors are larger; competitive advantage as Average, supported by patents and OEM programme positions but without evidence of a margin premium; and business diversification as Average, because end markets and regions are spread but one customer is 18% of sales and the products depend on combustion engines. Cost and capex flexibility is Average, because capital expenditure fell by 33.33% between FY2023 and the last twelve months while employee costs keep rising; margin stability is Average, because EBITDA margin held between 12.00% and 12.64% but 2026 gains lean on tariff timing; and free cash flow stability is Average, because conversion ranged from 23.81% to 47.21%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q3; calculation Q9; calculation Q10; calculation Q18; calculation Q1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average: the company issued USD 975 million of notes in 2024 and holds BB+ and Ba1 ratings with stable outlooks as of the FY2025 annual report, but no market quote or current agency report is supplied and the issuer's fair-value estimate of its debt fell to USD 967 million, only USD 1 million above carrying value, from a USD 47 million premium at the end of 2025. Liquidity is Strong before the stoba payment, with USD 813 million against USD 124 million of current debt, but the figure after the payment is not established. Financial policy and governance is Average, reflecting a Medium governance rating from Business & governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation Q16; calculation Q17; calculation Q25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are the aftermarket profit share, cash generation and long-dated debt; the constraints are returns above free cash flow, tariff-dependent earnings and customer concentration; the trend is stable earnings with leverage above its FY2023 level; and the key missing datapoints are stoba's financials, covenant definitions and a maturity schedule at 30 September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation Q7; calculation Q11; calculation Q12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The next 12 to 24 months are expected to be earnings-positive but volume-negative. Management expects light vehicle volumes to fall by mid-single digit percentages and commercial vehicle volumes by low-single digit percentages in its key markets in 2026, yet expects currency, efficiencies and share gains to more than offset that, and in October 2026 raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 500 million to USD 520 million from USD 485 million to USD 515 million, including stoba. The guidance implies USD 120 million to USD 140 million of adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter against USD 116 million a year earlier, which tests whether stoba adds earnings; adjusted free cash flow guidance of USD 220 million to USD 250 million compares with USD 212 million in FY2025 and with returns of USD 198 million in the nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q320268kex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation Q21; calculation Q28; calculation Q11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years management expects commercial-vehicle share gains, vehicle-parc growth that supports aftermarket demand, hybrid and alternative-fuel products and aerospace and defence growth, while the risk factors name faster electric-vehicle adoption as the main adverse case. Tailwinds therefore support the aftermarket profit pool and diversify away from light-vehicle combustion, and the headwinds are tariff reversal, OEM softness and the 2028 revolver and 2029 note maturities, which stay manageable if cash generation holds near FY2025 levels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_phin-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation Q15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with the softer original-equipment market that management already expects, continuing into 2027 while tariff-timing gains reverse as refunds are returned to customers. The first operating break would be Power Systems, where third-quarter 2026 segment adjusted operating income already fell USD 8 million and the margin slipped to 12.1% from 13.3%. Lower volume at that margin, with overhead fixed, would cut EBITDA and free cash flow; in FY2023, the weakest year shown, free cash flow was USD 100 million, which still covered dividends. If buybacks continued at the 2026 pace of USD 165 million over nine months, the shortfall would be met from cash and the revolver, lifting net leverage above the pro forma 1.64x, with the revolver maturing in about 19 months and the 2029 secured notes after that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q8; calculation Q9; calculation Q12; calculation Q15; calculation Q6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has levers: buybacks of USD 165 million in the nine months of 2026 are discretionary with USD 151 million of authorisation left, capital expenditure has already fallen to USD 100 million over the last twelve months from USD 150 million, and the dividend costs USD 33 million for nine months. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress if buybacks are cut early, because USD 813 million of liquidity before the stoba payment and no sizeable maturity before July 2028 give time; it would not be sufficient if returns and a debt-funded acquisition coincided with a deeper volume fall. The observable triggers are Power Systems margin below 10.8%, quarterly returns above adjusted free cash flow, and a revolver balance above USD 123 million after the stoba payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation Q10; calculation Q11; calculation Q16; calculation Q26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_phin-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Phinia presents an adequate business profile supported by an aftermarket arm that earns 49.17% of segment profit from 37.95% of sales, but credit quality is constrained by shareholder returns that match or exceed free cash flow, earnings that lean on tariff timing and currency, and one customer at 18% of sales. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow was positive in every period shown and spending can be cut. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the July 2028 revolver before the 2029 secured notes approach and on leverage staying near 1.64x pro forma. The primary downside path is a softer original-equipment market with reversing tariff gains and continued buybacks. Further analysis would require stoba's financials, the covenant definitions and a maturity schedule at the latest balance sheet. Top risk: shareholder returns and debt-funded acquisitions lifting leverage before the 2028 and 2029 maturities.
